description:
Found while doing fz-5xp.3 (declared extern ABI).

`Kernel` declares symbols that DO NOT EXIST as callable functions:

    extern "C" fn fz_op_lt_bb(binary, binary) :: bool
    extern "C" fn fz_op_eq(any, any) :: bool
    extern "C" fn fz_op_identical(any, any) :: bool
    ... every fz_op_{lt,lte,gt,gte}_{ii,ff,bb,if,fi}, eq/neq/identical

None of them is in `resolve_symbol`'s native table (`src/ir_interp/extern_call.rs`)
and none is a real Rust `extern "C"` function. They work only because BOTH doors
intercept them by name before the extern lane is reached:

  * native: the if-chain in `native_codegen/prim.rs::lower_prim`
  * interp: `eval_interp_operator_extern`

So the declaration is a fiction that types the surface, and the intercept is the
implementation. Nothing checks that the two agree. If an intercept is narrowed
-- an arity guard, a lowering that bails to the generic path, a new call shape --
the declaration says the fallback is legal, and the fallback fails at dlsym, far
from the cause.

The declared TYPES are a second fiction. `fz_op_lt_bb(binary, binary)` would
marshal its arguments to `*const u8` on the generic path, which is not what the
comparison wants; the `fz` ABI added in fz-5xp.3 would give it value refs but
also prepend a process argument that `fz_value_cmp_ref` does not take. Neither
declared convention describes what these actually are, which is the real signal:
they are INTRINSICS wearing extern syntax (the fz-5xp.3 design comment calls this
category (b) and says, correctly, not to fold it into the ABI).

WHAT WOULD FIX IT. Either:

  (a) a test that walks every extern the runtime library declares and asserts it
      is EITHER resolvable as a symbol on both doors OR claimed by an intercept
      on both doors -- the pairing is then checked rather than assumed; or

  (b) a declaration form that says "intrinsic", so the surface stops claiming a
      C symbol and a wire type that nothing honours, and the generic path can
      refuse an intrinsic outright.

(b) is the correct-by-construction answer and subsumes (a). It also gives
fz-5xp.21 a place to record which questions are answered by an intrinsic on each
door.

NOT URGENT: today the failure mode is loud (`dlsym: symbol not found`), not
silent. Filed so it is not rediscovered.

Related: fz-5xp.3 (the ABI is now declared), fz-5xp.21 (one question, N
implementations), fz-5xp.20 (inlining wrappers over intrinsics).
title: Runtime-library externs whose declaration no symbol backs are unguarded
